learningObjective: Compare NVLink and PCIe bandwidth for inter-GPU communication and reason about ring-AllReduce throughput.
profileData: Ring-AllReduce of a 1 GiB FP16 tensor across 8 H100 SXM5 nodes fully connected by NVLink 4.0. Same experiment across 8 H100 PCIe cards on PCIe Gen4 x16.
stem: You have two 8-GPU setups: (i) H100 SXM5 with NVLink 4.0 (per-GPU aggregate ≈ 900 GB/s bidirectional) and (ii) H100 PCIe cards on PCIe Gen4 x16 (≈ 25 GB/s per-direction between neighbors, no NVLink). You run ring-AllReduce on a 1 GiB FP16 tensor. Which comparison is closest to correct in the bandwidth-bound regime?

options.text: NVLink is roughly 1–2 orders of magnitude faster than PCIe here because ring-AllReduce is limited by the slowest inter-GPU link; NVLink's ~900 GB/s bidirectional per GPU vs PCIe's ~25 GB/s per direction dominates the collective time.
Both complete in the same time because ring-AllReduce total bytes are dominated by the sum, independent of link technology.
PCIe is faster because CPU-mediated routing bypasses the NVLink handshake overhead, giving lower latency for tensors above 512 MiB.
NVLink and PCIe give the same throughput per direction; only bidirectional aggregate differs and AllReduce uses one direction at a time.

explanation: Ring-AllReduce sends 2(P−1)/P × N bytes per link at bandwidth-limited steady state, where N is tensor size and P is number of GPUs. The runtime is roughly N / effective_link_BW. With NVLink 4.0's ~900 GB/s bidirectional aggregate per GPU vs PCIe Gen4 x16's ~25 GB/s per direction, the effective inter-GPU bandwidth differs by more than an order of magnitude. So NVLink completes the collective substantially faster. Options A, C, D contain factual or reasoning errors.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: for a bandwidth-bound ring, NVLink's link BW is roughly 10–30× PCIe's, giving a corresponding wall-time advantage.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: bandwidth-bound collective time is proportional to bytes / link BW; identical time would require identical BW.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: PCIe with CPU-mediated routing is slower, not faster, and NVLink does not require a per-transfer handshake that would offset its bandwidth advantage.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: NVLink's per-direction bandwidth already exceeds PCIe's by an order of magnitude; the bidirectional aggregate is not the only difference.

assumptions: Ring-AllReduce in the bandwidth-bound regime (tensor large enough that latency terms are negligible).
PCIe topology has no NVLink or NVSwitch fabric between GPUs.
NVLink 4.0 per-GPU aggregate ~ 900 GB/s bidirectional (H100 SXM5 typical published number).
nonImplications: Does not imply NVLink is always 10–30× faster; small message sizes are latency-bound, where the gap may narrow.
Does not imply the exact speedup ratio; effective BW is affected by NCCL algorithm, topology, and buffer chunking.

distractorRationales.B: Ignores link bandwidth in bandwidth-bound analysis.

performanceClaim.scope: 8-GPU H100 ring-AllReduce, 1 GiB FP16 tensor, bandwidth-bound regime
